name: Distributions and Limit Theorems
description: Meet the named distributions and see why averages settle and sums look normal.

skills.dl-lln: Law of large numbers and inequalities

requires.why: Uses variance and standard deviation to describe the binomial, geometric and Poisson distributions.
Derives the Poisson as a binomial limit using e as the limit of compounding.
Finds probabilities as areas under densities and evaluates them with antiderivatives.
Extends joint tables, independence and conditional expectation to joint densities.
Changes variables in a double integral with the Jacobian determinant to transform densities.
Gamma and Beta integrals and convolutions need substitution and improper integrals.

lessonNames.l3-rare-events: Rare events in a fixed window
lessonNames.l12-skill-or-luck: How many trades until skill shows?

lessonObjectives.l1-counting-successes: Derive the binomial distribution from independent trials.
lessonObjectives.l2-first-success: Use the geometric distribution and derive its mean.
lessonObjectives.l3-rare-events: Use the Poisson distribution as a limit of the binomial.
lessonObjectives.l4-without-replacement: Use the hypergeometric distribution and compare it with the binomial.
lessonObjectives.l5-probability-as-area: Read a density and find probabilities as areas under it.
lessonObjectives.l6-uniform-exponential: Use the uniform and exponential distributions, and meet memorylessness.
lessonObjectives.l7-bell-curve: Standardise a normal variable and find its probabilities.
lessonObjectives.l8-lognormal: Model a price with the lognormal distribution.
lessonObjectives.l9-averages-settle: See the law of large numbers in simulation, then state it.
lessonObjectives.l11-sums-look-normal: Watch sums from any distribution become normal, and state the central limit theorem.
lessonObjectives.l12-skill-or-luck: Use the central limit theorem to judge whether an average return is real.
lessonObjectives.l13-approximating-binomial: Approximate binomial probabilities with a normal curve and a continuity correction.
lessonObjectives.l14-joint-densities: Find probabilities, marginals and conditional densities from a joint density, and test independence.
lessonObjectives.l15-new-variables: Find the density of a transformed variable, with $|dx/dy|$ in one dimension and a Jacobian in two.
lessonObjectives.l16-adding-densities: Find the density of a sum of independent variables by convolution.
lessonObjectives.l17-smallest-and-largest: Find the distributions of the minimum, the maximum and the $k$th smallest of independent draws.
lessonObjectives.l18-gamma-beta: Use the Gamma, Beta, chi-square and t distributions and the stories that produce them.
lessonObjectives.l19-generating-functions: Use moment generating functions to find moments, identify a sum’s distribution and bound a tail.
